newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Some basis offers move higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Some basis offers move higher.

text.p: Expectations for a near-term drop in the pace of the U.S. soybean crush pushed some truck and rail basis offers higher Wednesday, cash sources said.
"They're calling the basis higher here again today with all the downtime coming up in the first half of May," said one southeastern dealer.
Most in the trade are looking for the National Oilseed Processors weekly crushing pace to fall slightly below last week's pace of 25.644 million bushel.
Trade was quiet because the increase in basis and CBOT soymeal prices meant prices were too dear for end-users.
"With the board up the way it is, people are just trying to figure out what to do next," said an Indiana dealer.
At 1029 CDT, CBOT July soymeal was up $5.60 at $284.30 per ton. During morning trade, July achieved a high of $285.50.
